# ᝯㄝₓ Orphan Cleanup

Requires Stash 0.31.0 or newer and [ᝯㄝₓ Core](../GTTx-Core/README.md), installed and enabled alongside
it. A source index (Stash's Settings → Plugins → Available Plugins) installs Core for you; a hand
copy must copy the `GTTxCore` folder too. Without Core it does nothing but say so, in red under its name on Settings → Plugins and
Settings → Tasks and in the browser console.

Which tags, performers, studios and groups does nothing use any more?

Stash can sort each of its lists by scene count, one type at a time, and each count is only one of
the ways an [<abbr title="One item in a Stash library - a scene, image, gallery, performer, studio, group, tag or scene marker.">entity</abbr>](../GLOSSARY.md#entity) is used. This plugin asks all of them, for the four types at once, and deletes
the ones you tick.

## Usage

**Settings → Tasks → Plugin Tasks → Find Orphans...**

The dialog lists every orphan it finds, under one heading per type, each a link with its hover card
and its id. **Nothing is ticked**: tick what to delete, or press **Select All**, then press **Delete...**
twice - the first press only asks.

**Show:** above the list has a switch for each type it holds, with its count. Untick one to hide
that type: **Select All**, **Unselect All**, the count on **Delete...** and the delete itself then
leave it alone, ticked or not, until it is shown again.

## What counts as an orphan

Every count Stash keeps for the entity is 0 - counted directly, not through child tags or child
studios:

| Type | Used when it has |
|---|---|
| Tag | a scene, a marker (as its primary tag or one of its tags), an image, a gallery, a performer, a studio or a group |
| Performer | a scene, an image, a gallery or a group |
| Studio | a scene, an image, a gallery or a group |
| Group | a scene |

**Never listed**, whatever the settings: a tag a ᝯㄝₓ plugin works by - one its settings name, by
name or alias, or one whose name starts with the collection's own mark.

## Exclusion Filters

What else is left out is set in the **Exclusion Filters** row on this plugin's settings
(Settings → Plugins), in a dialog:

| Setting | Default | Never lists |
|---|---|---|
| Leave Out Favorites | On | a favorite tag, performer or studio (a group has no favorite) |
| Leave Out Anything Linked to a [<abbr title="A shared online database of scene, performer and studio metadata that Stash matches against and scrapes from; StashDB is the best-known one.">Stash-Box</abbr>](../GLOSSARY.md#stash-box) | Off | a tag, performer or studio holding a [<abbr title="The link from an entity in your library to its entry on a stash-box: the box's address and the entry's id.">stash-id</abbr>](../GLOSSARY.md#stash-id) |
| Leave Out Entities Carrying This Tag | `ᱜ╦╦🞮✅DoNotCleanUp⚠∙` | a performer, studio or group carrying the tag, every tag below it at any depth, and the tag itself - matched by its name or an alias |
| Leave Out Entities Marked via This Custom Field | `ᱜ╦╦🞮_Do_Not_Clean_Up` | a tag, performer, studio or group holding the field, whatever its value |
| Leave Out Anything With Children | On | a tag with child tags, a studio with child studios, a group with [<abbr title="A group (formerly a movie) collects scenes in order; a group can hold other groups, its sub-groups.">sub-groups</abbr>](../GLOSSARY.md#group) |
| Leave Out Anything With a Parent | Off | a tag with a [<abbr title="Tags nest: a tag's parents and sub-tags, and everything above (ancestors) or below (descendants) it.">parent</abbr>](../GLOSSARY.md#parent) tag, a studio with a parent studio, a group inside another group |

An empty name turns its filter off. The tag is matched as Stash's own filters match a name: letters
A-Z in any case, other letters exactly, and `_` or `%` standing for any character. A tag named that
no tag has leaves nothing out, and the dialog's log says so unless the box holds its default. The custom field is described in [Custom Fields Bulk
Editor](../GTTx-CustomFieldsBulkEditor/README.md)'s description [<abbr title="The tag Custom Fields Bulk Editor keeps the custom-field descriptions in.">store</abbr>](../GLOSSARY.md#store) as a scan starts, as
De-Spicer's are.

With **Leave Out Anything With Children** on, a namespace tag nothing is assigned to stays off the
list. Off, it is listed, and deleting it leaves its children without that parent; Undo puts them
back under it. With **Leave Out Anything With a Parent** off, a tag with nothing on it under a parent
tag is an orphan - otherwise no leaf tag in a tag tree would ever be one.

The line above the list says how many unused entities each reason left out. A delete is checked
against the filters the list was drawn by; a change saved since counts from the next **Rescan**.

## Deleting, and Undo

**Backing up your database first is strongly recommended**, and the dialog's head says so.

Each ticked entity is **checked again** just before it goes, in batches: one that has been used
since the list was drawn - a scene tagged in another tab - is left alone, and the log says why.
The rest are deleted through Stash's own bulk delete, and **Stop** halts after the batch in flight.

Every delete is recorded in ᝯㄝₓ Core's [Undo History](../GTTx-Core/README.md#undo-history),
under this plugin's name, whatever Core's **Record Deletes** setting says: each entity is read whole
before it goes, its picture too with **Record Pictures** on. **Undo**, in this dialog while it stays
open, makes every one again from the history - newest first, each under a new id - and the undo is
recorded in turn. After the dialog has closed, the same runs are undone from Undo History. Not
everything can be undone there: see [what Undo History cannot undo](../GTTx-Core/README.md#what-undo-history-cannot-undo).

**Copy log** and **Save log** hand over the list, with what was ticked and deleted, and every
message. **Rescan** lists the orphans as the library is now; Undo keeps what it can still reach.

## Relationship to the other plugins in this repo

It takes the shared bulk-edit [<abbr title="The flag a plugin holds while it writes, so the others do not react to its writes.">lease</abbr>](../GLOSSARY.md#lease) while it deletes, so the other plugins' automatic modes stand
down, and it reads their settings - through ᝯㄝₓ Core - only to leave the tags they work by alone.

## Notes and limitations

- **Scenes, images, galleries and markers are never deleted**: their files are your library.
- **Nothing outside Stash's counts is seen.** A tag named only in a saved filter, or kept for a
  collection you fill now and then, is listed when it is empty - which is why nothing starts ticked.
- **An undone delete comes back under a new id**: a bookmark or a link to the old page does not
  follow it.

## Troubleshooting

**The task button does nothing.** The click is handled in the browser - there is no server-side
job behind it. If Stash instead shows an "added job to queue" toast, the page is running a script
that does not recognize the button; reload the page.

### Checking which version is actually running

**A red banner says the page is running an older script**, on the settings group and in the
dialog, each with a red **Reload UI** button. Press it, or reload the page - see [the
stale-script banner and the Reload UI button](../GTTx-Core/README.md#the-stale-script-banner-and-the-reload-ui-button).

## Installing

Copy the `GTTx-OrphanCleanup` folder into your Stash plugins directory
(`<stash-config-dir>/plugins/`) and press **Reload plugins** in Settings → Plugins.
